headline: Growth holds steady as operating leverage lifts profit
summary_short: Okta's fiscal Q2 revenue rose 11.2% y/y to $765M and operating income grew 43.6% to $56M as G&A spend held flat; net income rose 19.4% to $74M and diluted EPS grew to $0.42 from $0.35.
summary_long: Subscription revenue growth was driven by more users and additional-solution sales to existing customers, reflected in a 107% net retention rate (up from 106%) and 5,180 customers with >$100K ACV (from 4,870). Gross margin held roughly flat near 78% as higher hosting and labor costs offset revenue growth. Operating income grew faster than revenue as G&A improved to 13% of revenue (from 15%), even as S&M rose to 36% (from 34%) on higher labor, marketing and travel costs. Total and current RPO grew to $4,719M and $2,499M. Okta repurchased $241M of stock under its $1B buyback program and generated $277M of operating cash flow. No forward revenue or EPS guidance is stated in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Revenue growth continued on retention and new-customer additions while G&A spend efficiency expanded operating leverage, lifting operating and net income faster than revenue.
Subscription revenue growth was primarily due to more users and additional solutions sold to existing customers plus new customer additions, reflected in the 107% net retention rate.
Cost of subscription revenue rose on $8M more hosting fees and $3M more labor costs, partially offsetting revenue growth; subscription gross margin held roughly flat.
G&A held roughly flat in dollars and fell to 13% of revenue (from 15%) on spend efficiency, offsetting S&M rising to 36% of revenue (from 34%) on higher labor, marketing and travel costs.
Net income growth outpaced revenue on the operating-income improvement plus a lower effective tax rate (4.6% vs 8.5% a year ago) following favorable impacts from 2025 U.S. tax legislation.
EPS growth (+20%) outpaced net income growth (+19%) as diluted share count fell versus a year ago on the ongoing $1B share buyback program.
